title: Bridleway LLM paper-sprint notes
content:
(quick sprint dump) 3-hour reading + tiny experiments. goal: collect deployability heuristics we can try on Dedicated + Private for low-cost fallbacks

Context and why I care:
- Running into customer reports where tails of token-latency spike after 3-5min sessions in Dedicated pools. Not easy repro in local rigs. Need lightweight probes and a set of actionable mitigations that ops + solutions can try without full model retrain.
- Want checklist that can be executed by on-call or SE in a 30–90min window. Make it reproducible and scriptable.

Papers skimmed (notes in my words):
1) "KV-Compression for Continuous Long Contexts" (arXiv, 2026)
   - idea: compress old KV blocks via learned projection + residual indexing; cheap to decode for next queries.
   - implication: for long-lived sessions, we can reduce memory pressure and avoid kernel thrash that sometimes shows up as latency spikes.
   - quick thought: prototype offline with a 4k->512 block compressor and measure decode time on T4/RTX6000. If decode < 1ms per token frame, acceptable.

2) "Runtime Fallback and Model Variant Routing" (ML Sys conf)
   - adaptive routing to lower-precision variant when latency SLOs threatened, but must keep semantic constraints.
   - important: need quality-aware metric (embedding-distance, LM-score over held prompt), not just token-level perplexity.
   - OPS play: define a fallback policy that is triggered by 95th percentile token-latency and verified by a cheap eval on a micro-prompt set (<=10 toks).

3) "Shard-aware KV Eviction Strategies" (workshop paper)
   - eviction should consider cross-shard reuse probability; naive LRU across shards awful.
   - experiment: simulate shard collisions using our trace library (trace-gen) to see how many misses when we clamp KV store to 20% of peak.

Quick heuristics / checklist for an on-call run (30–90m):
- Gather: latest SAC (serving-adjacent-collector) trace for offending interval, include host-level metrics (GPU mem clock, sm utilization, ctx switches).
- Repro: pick a 1-min representative session, replay in staging with identical batch sizes + seq length distribution and record per-token latencies.
- Probe: toggle KV-cache TTL (full, half, 25%) and measure 95th percentile change. Log kernel durations.
- Fallback policy smoke: flip to q4f variant on a canary and run micro-eval: make sure embedding-distance to golden <= 0.05.
- Eviction test: artificially constrain KV store capacity and run trace-gen to measure miss amplification.
- If kernel thrash suspected: try pinning CPU affinity for IO threads and reduce prefetch workers by 50% and re-run.

Tiny experiment I ran while reading (very rough):
- Setup: local small-Llama 7B quantized with our q4f backend on a single A10G. Load a 6-minute synthetic session with 8k total tokens.
- Variation: baseline vs simple prefix-compression (gzip-like on older KVs) vs projection compress (toy linear projection).
- Result (local rough): prefix-compress reduces GPU memory by ~12% and lowers 95th token-latency by 9% (likely due to less context copying). Linear projection toy reduced mem 18% but added ~0.7ms per-token decode overhead (not terrible).
- Note: these are noisy; need multi-run and real traces. But promising signal that cheap compression could help tails.

Hypotheses to prioritize (ranked):
- H1: Most customer tail latency events are due to KV memory churn + cross-shard evictions rather than raw compute saturation. Low-effort mitigation: TTL + smaller prefix retention.
- H2: Lightweight model-variant fallback with a micro-eval gate will maintain perceived quality while shaving tails when capacity constrained.
- H3: IO/worker thread misconfiguration explodes tail latency under mixed small/large sessions. Provide a standard flavor for Dedicated pools.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- A: Scripted repro harness that can: pull SAC traces, parameterize TTL/eviction, run in staging and produce a one-page report. (owner: Owen)
- B: Micro-eval set: curate 50 micro-prompts across chat/qa/code; baseline quality scores for main models + q4f + q3 variants. (owner: Mira)
- C: Benchmark decode overhead for projection-based compression across A10/A100/T4 and add to perf playbook. (owner: me; target: 10/15)
- D: Draft an ops-runbook for fallback toggles + safety checks; include Slack shortcodes and alert playbook. (owner: eng-sre)

Questions / open puzzles I want to follow up on:
- Can we instrument per-kv-block reuse probability live (cheaply) to make eviction decisions data-driven?
- Are there pathological prompt patterns (like streaming code deltas) that cause predictable thrash? If so, can we detect with micro-signatures?
- How does prefix compression interact with function-calling structured outputs (weird token alignment issues)?

Snippets / quick commands (for my reproducibility later):
- SAC pull: sac-client dump --span="2026-09-28T03:20:00Z/2026-09-28T03:30:00Z" --filter="pool:dedicated-eastus-3" > session.json
- trace-gen run: python tools/trace_gen.py --input session.json --kv-cap=0.2 --out results/kvcap-0.2.json
- micro-eval runner: ./bin/micro_eval --model main --variant q4f --prompts microset.json --metrics embedding,rank

References I bookmarked while reading:
- simon-lee-2026-kv-compress.pdf (local note: see section 4 for decode perf table)
- runtime-fallbacks-mlsys-2026 (conference slides)
- eviction-topologies-workshop-2026 (code: GH link in slack thread)

Random heuristics I liked and want to codify in the perf playbook:
- "short first" scheduling: prioritize small interactive requests through a fast path queue to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- micro-eval gating for any model-variant switch (<= 10 prompts, precomputed thresholds).
- cap KV retention per-session based on sliding-window reuse rate, not absolute token count.

Notes to self: keep this doc alive as an index of reproducible mitigations. Once we have the repro harness and microset, convert to playbook template for SEs. Share to #runtime-research and ping Owen/Mira for sync.
